prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map lays out a checkout counter directly below and in front of the camera wearer, with a cash register (bottom-left), a tall brown paper bag (centre-right), a jar (far bottom-left), and a red basket (far right) all glowing brightly in the foreground at roughly 0.4–0.8 m away, within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person across the counter. Behind the register at roughly 0.9–1.2 m stands a person on the upper-left facing toward the camera wearer, positioned about 0.3–0.5 m behind the register and adjacent to the paper bag, while a display case sits further back on the upper-right at roughly 1.8–2.5 m. The register and counter edge partially occlude the person's lower body, and in frames 1–4 the upper portion of the person's head is cut off by the top frame boundary before coming partially into view in frame 5 as the camera tilts slightly upward and the person leans slightly forward with both hands reaching down to the register drawer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the recessed register cash drawer from its raised keypad housing and highlights the hollow interior depth of the open paper bag and red basket. However, the map looks unreliable in the dark background gap between the person and the paper bag (which collapses to uniform black) and on the flat countertop paper under the bag, which blends smoothly into the bag's base without a sharp depth boundary.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map identifies only a sparse subset of the scene across the five frames: the person standing behind the counter on the upper-left (0.9–1.2 m away, facing the camera wearer) is segmented in frames 2, 4, and 5, while foreground objects at 0.4–0.8 m (all within arm's reach of both people) are intermittently segmented beneath misclassified labels. Specifically, the jar on the far left is labelled 'bottle' (frame 1) or 'cup' (frame 5), the cash register in the lower-left is labelled 'laptop' (frame 1) or split into 'keyboard' and 'book' (frame 2), the tall brown paper bag to its right is labelled 'book' across frames 1–4, the cash notes at the bottom-centre are labelled 'cup' (frame 1), and the background display case on the upper-right (1.8–2.5 m away) is labelled 'tv' in frame 5. Across the sequence, the masks reflect the camera tilting slightly upward by frame 5—bringing more of the person's upper torso and neck into the mask while the paper bag on the right drops out of segmentation entirely—and capture the occlusion of the person's lower torso behind the register in frames 2 and 4. While the segmentation map provides sharp outer silhouettes for the person's torso and shoulders against the dark background that are low-contrast in RGB, it is highly unreliable in both class labelling and temporal consistency, completely missing the person in frames 1 and 3 and the red basket on the far right in all frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the skeleton and hands of the single person standing behind the counter on the upper-left (roughly 0.9–1.2 m from the camera wearer), who faces directly toward the camera wearer with both hands positioned within arm's reach of the cash register drawer (0.5–0.8 m from the camera wearer) just to the left of the paper bag. In frames 1–4, because the person's head is mostly cropped out at the top edge of the image and the register occludes their waist, the map detects only their raised right hand (magenta) hovering just above the open cash drawer—along with a false-positive miniature yellow body skeleton on the far-left jar in frame 1. Across frames 1 to 4, this right hand shifts slightly downward and rightward relative to the frame as the camera view tilts up, and in frame 5 the full upper-body skeleton (shoulders, torso, both arms, and five facial keypoints at the top edge) appears as the person's head enters the frame and both hands reach down into the register drawer about 0.2 m apart. The pose map makes the exact 2D joint articulation of the fingers on the right hand and the symmetric forward-facing shoulder alignment in frame 5 much clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, it is unreliable in frames 1–4 where it completely fails to detect the visible torso, arms, and left hand resting on the side of the register, and where it hallucinates a tiny body skeleton on the jar in frame 1.
